correctness.rationale: The full proof in RESULT.md derives both KL functionals from Fourier aliasing and harmonic logarithmic integrals. Differentiation yields an exact one-variable sign factor; global minima follow from complete stationary-branch analysis and endpoint divergence. A unique simultaneous tie equation gives all critical radii, and a strict convexity argument ensures they are interior. The m>=3 large-order law follows from a central second-difference expansion. Standalone finite diagnostics compare formulas with quadrature, but are not relied on as proofs.

value.rationale: The regular-polygon Poisson compression problem is a natural circular information-geometry analogue of single-component mixture reduction. It exhibits two qualitatively distinct symmetry-breaking transition orders, an explicit universal threshold sequence, and opposite outcomes when KL arguments are reversed. The exact m^-2 boundary scale and complete optimizer counts are meaningful structural information, not isolated numerical cases or a routine alteration of L2 findings.
